problem: Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded between $y={x}^{2}-5$ and $y=4x?$

feedback.problem: Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded between $y={x}^{2}+2x-9$ and $y=2x+7?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's draw the graphs of the two functions:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/2514c3e7bf5352dbe26dddc479f66042b3736b93f82b97a60850f768a89a4e17.png)

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we equate the two functions and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x-9 & =2x+7 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $x=-4$ to $x=4.$
To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/560fb0937828d5afb5de9593280a1177773598c5d3534ee26318e0bc2788f5ab.png)

 

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y={x}^{2}+2x-9,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=2x+7.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}[\,(2x+7)-({x}^{2}+2x-9)\,]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}(-{x}^{2}+16)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}(16-{x}^{2})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
